newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil easies on selling side.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil easies on selling side.

text.p: The European low sulphur straight-run market was a shade weaker on Thursday with sellers again cutting their asking price a notch but no one seen picking up cargoes, traders said.
One seller was offering at $99 a tonne and a second at $98/$99, $1 to $2 off their previous price tag for low sulphur straight-run. Buyers were a few dollars lower.
Despite crude's relatively stability "it is a terrible market for straight-run, there's not that much demand", one trader said.
"Last month we had good buying interest but now it is not that good," he added.
A second seller said he would do $99 "but I don't see buyers around".
However, some sellers said a little buying interest was coming in from the United States.
Traders said refiners were finding it hard to value straight-run at the moment, with crude prices in helter-skelter.

"The market is very jumpy. It is very difficult to put a value on straight-run when crude is down in the morning, then up in the afternoon, then down again in the evening like we saw yesterday," one trader said.
